Rotate players between sections after each block.
coachingPoints: Close each receiver as the football is arriving.
Protect the inside leading lane.
Defenders behind the football must scan for the next lead before the current disposal.
Communicate runners moving between sections.
Avoid following one opponent so far that the next section becomes exposed.
Recover behind the football after being bypassed.
Use pressure on the receiver to make the next kick predictable.
Maintain connection between defensive sections.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders close receivers before they can turn.
Whether the next lead is identified early.
Whether handovers are communicated.
Whether gaps appear between defensive sections.
Whether beaten defenders recover behind the football.
Whether pressure makes the next disposal predictable.
progressions: Remove section boundaries.
Allow attackers to run and carry.
Add full legal tackling.
Introduce a wide switch option.
Start from an unpredictable turnover.
regressions: Require attackers to use predetermined receivers.
Allow the coach to pause before each new lead.
successIndicators: Close lead-up receivers before they turn.
Recover and maintain connection behind the football.
matchApplication: Teams often advance through repeated short marks and lead-up targets. This drill teaches defenders to pressure each possession while remaining aware of the next receiver and preserving connection between defensive lines.

title: High-to-Low Defender Rotation
primarySkill: Rotating defensive players between high pressure and deeper cover positions.
objective: Develop the movement and communication required for one defender to press forward while another rotates behind to preserve defensive depth.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Divide the defensive team into a high line and a low line.
Position attackers between and around the two defensive lines.
Begin with the attacking team controlling possession at one end.
Nominate a communicator in the low defensive line.
Allow the defence to press only when a clear opportunity appears.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team moves the football through the area.
When a high defender leaves the line to pressure, a low defender rotates across and behind that space.
If the football moves past the high line, the pressing defender recovers into the low line.
Another defender may then step forward to apply pressure.
The defence continually exchanges high and low responsibilities as possession moves.
Attackers score by moving through the target gate.
Defenders score one point for forcing play backwards and two points for an intercept.
Teams rotate roles after three-minute blocks.
coachingPoints: No defender should press forward unless depth is protected behind them.
The low line must communicate who is covering the released space.
Pressing defenders recover through the inside after being bypassed.
The next defender steps only when the recovering player is moving into cover.
Maintain staggered depth rather than two flat lines.
Scan before leaving the line.
Avoid several defenders stepping forward at once.
Continue rotating until possession is won or the attack is stopped.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the pressing defender has cover behind.
Whether low defenders rotate early.
Whether the released space remains protected.
Whether beaten high defenders recover into the low line.
Whether lines remain staggered.
Whether multiple players step without communication.
progressions: Remove the nominated lines.
Add full tackling.
Increase attacking speed.
Begin from rapid turnovers.
Add a forward behind the deepest line.
regressions: The coach calls which defender must step.
successIndicators: Press forward only when cover is available.
Rotate a teammate behind the pressure action.
Recover into deeper positions after being bypassed.
Exchange high and low roles without losing connection.
matchApplication: Defensive systems require players to step out and pressure while teammates replace the space behind them. Effective rotation allows the team to remain aggressive without exposing dangerous space behind the first defender.

title: Defending the Run-Through from Behind
primarySkill: Identifying and defending an opponent running forward from behind the ball.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to recognise a late runner entering the play from behind and prevent that player from receiving uncontested possession through the defensive line.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position an attacking ball carrier and receiver ahead of a defensive line.
Place a third attacker 10–15 metres behind the football as the late runner.
Position three defenders across the width of the area.
Place a scoring gate behind the defenders.
The late runner may enter through any lane.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves laterally or forward while looking for the receiver.
The late runner accelerates from behind and attempts to run through the defensive line.
The deepest or weak-side defender calls the runner.
The nearest defender tracks or hands the runner to a teammate.
The remaining defenders continue applying pressure to the football and protecting the original receiver.
Attackers attempt to score through the gate.
Defenders score one point for denying the late runner and two points for a turnover.
Reset with the runner beginning from a different side.
coachingPoints: Scan behind and beside the football, not only at the current receiver.
The deepest defender must identify the runner early.
Communicate the runner’s location and direction.
Protect the inside lane before following the runner wide.
Decide whether to track directly or hand responsibility to a teammate.
Maintain pressure on the ball carrier so the release is delayed.
Avoid two defenders abandoning the same space.
Recover goal-side if the runner breaks through.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan for movement from behind.
Whether the late runner is communicated early.
Whether responsibility is clear.
Whether pressure remains on the ball carrier.
Whether central space is protected.
Whether defenders recover if the runner receives.
progressions: Add a second late runner.
Allow the ball carrier to kick over the defensive line.
Introduce full tackling.
Begin from a turnover with defenders facing the wrong direction.
Remove predetermined match-ups.
regressions: Allow the coach to call the runner.
successIndicators: Scan for runners arriving from behind.
Assign responsibility without losing defensive shape.
Maintain pressure on the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Midfielders and half-backs often run from behind the football to create an extra attacker. This drill teaches defenders to recognise those movements before the runner penetrates the defensive line.

title: Defensive Fold Around the Contest
primarySkill: Folding defenders around the back of a moving contest.
objective: Develop the movement pattern in which defenders recover around the back of a contest to rebuild pressure, cover and balance on the new ball side.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a square area with a target gate on each side.
Begin with a three-against-three contest near the centre.
Position two additional defenders on one side of the contest.
Position attacking support players around the remaining sides.
The coach begins with a ground ball or short disposal into the contest.
Explain that defenders on the old ball side must fold behind the contest when play moves away.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players contest possession in the centre.
When the football moves towards one side, the nearest defenders apply pressure.
Defenders left on the old ball side sprint around the back of the contest.
Those folding players become the new cover and balance defenders.
The attacking team attempts to exit through any gate.
Defenders score one point for completing the fold before the next disposal and two points for forcing a turnover.
After a turnover, the defence exits through the opposite gate.
Continue for 30–45 seconds before resetting.
coachingPoints: Fold behind the contest rather than running through congested traffic.
Recover through goal-side and central space.
The first folding player becomes cover; the next provides balance.
Communicate which player is pressuring and who is folding.
Move immediately when the football leaves the old side.
Maintain width after completing the fold.
Avoid all defenders arriving at the same point.
Continue folding as the contest changes direction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders react immediately when the football changes sides.
Whether players fold behind rather than through the contest.
Whether pressure, cover and balance are restored.
Whether players spread after completing the fold.
Whether communication identifies the new pressure defender.
Whether fatigue reduces defensive discipline.
progressions: Increase the work interval.
Add full match-like tackling.
Introduce a second football after a turnover.
Increase the playing area.
Require the defence to complete an attacking transition after winning possession.
regressions: Predetermine the direction of the first disposal.
Allow a brief pause before the fold.
Use touch pressure rather than tackling.
successIndicators: Recognise when they are on the old ball side.
Maintain defensive connection under repeated movement.
matchApplication: As contests move across the ground, defenders on the old side must recover around the back to support the new pressure point. Effective folding prevents the opposition from escaping into open space after the first contest.

title: Defensive Movement Fundamentals Assessment
primarySkill: Applying coordinated defensive movement principles during continuous play.
objective: Assess whether players can independently execute the defensive movement principles introduced in TD-021 to TD-029 during changing game situations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two-thirds of the ground with goals at one end and exit gates at the other.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Position defenders across multiple connected lines.
Prepare the following starting scenarios:
Lateral ball movement
A defender initially beaten outside
A give-and-go combination
A late runner from behind
Consecutive lead-up receivers
A contest changing sides
Assign coaches or leaders to assess specific movement behaviours.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each repetition from one of the prepared scenarios.
The attacking team attempts to move the football forward and score.
The defence must close space, track runners and maintain connected movement.
Opponents moving between areas must be tracked or handed over.
Defenders beaten on the outside must recover through the inside.
When the contest changes sides, old-side defenders fold behind the play.
After winning possession, defenders attempt to exit through a nominated gate.
Each repetition continues for 45–90 seconds before the next scenario begins.
coachingPoints: Close opponents with balanced footwork.
Move defensive lines as the football is being transferred.
Recover through goal-side central space when beaten.
Continue tracking opponents after they dispose.
Communicate every handover and late runner.
Rotate high pressure and deeper cover positions.
Fold behind contests as the football changes sides.
Maintain defensive shape while moving at match speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders close under control.
Whether lateral line movement remains connected.
Whether beaten players recover through the inside.
Whether give-and-go and late runners are tracked.
Whether opponents are handed over clearly.
Whether high and low defenders rotate.
Whether old-side defenders fold behind the contest.
Whether movement remains disciplined under fatigue.
Whether defenders communicate without coach prompting.
Whether a successful defensive action leads to a controlled exit.
progressions: Remove all coach-directed scenario information.
Use full match-like contact.
Introduce scoreboard and time pressure.
Add repeat entries after failed exits.
Require the defence to transition into a full forward entry after the stop.
regressions: Assess one movement principle at a time.
Pause between phases for defensive organisation.
Allow nominated leaders to direct movement.
successIndicators: Slide defensive lines in connection with the football.
Rotate between high pressure and low cover.
Fold around contests when play changes sides.
Maintain communication and structure under fatigue.
Win possession and complete an organised exit.
matchApplication: This assessment combines the movement behaviours required for effective team defence. It measures whether players can maintain structure while closing, recovering, tracking, rotating and folding during realistic changes in possession and field position.

title: Defensive Sprint-to-Set
primarySkill: Transitioning from recovery running into a balanced defensive position.
objective: Develop players’ ability to sprint back at high speed, identify the most dangerous threat and establish a balanced defensive position before applying pressure.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge and one main teaching point
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a scoring gate at one end.
Position two attackers approximately 20 metres from the gate.
Place one defender five to eight metres ahead of the attackers but facing away from goal.
The coach or feeder begins with a football outside the area.
On the coach’s signal, the attackers move towards goal while the defender turns and recovers.
Rotate players through attacking, defending and feeding roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach calls “turn” and releases the two attackers towards the scoring gate.
The defender turns, accelerates towards goal and scans over both shoulders.
The feeder disposes to either attacker.
The defender identifies the most dangerous attacker and establishes a goal-side position.
Before applying pressure, the defender decelerates into balanced footwork.
The attackers have six seconds to score through the gate.
The defender scores one point for delaying the attack and two points for preventing the score.
Reset from the opposite side after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Turn towards goal before locating opponents.
Accelerate immediately through the shortest central route.
Scan while running rather than waiting until reaching the contest.
Identify the opponent closest to goal or the most dangerous receiving lane.
Decelerate before engaging the attacker.
Establish goal-side position before attempting to win possession.
Use body position to force the attacker wider.
Communicate with any recovering teammate or goalkeeper behind the play.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders turn towards goal immediately.
Whether recovery occurs through the shortest central route.
Whether defenders scan during the sprint.
Whether the most dangerous attacker is identified.
Whether players decelerate into balanced defensive footwork.
Whether the attack is forced away from the central scoring line.
progressions: Add a second recovering defender.
Allow attackers to kick as well as handball.
Introduce full legal tackling.
Increase the defender’s starting deficit.
Begin from a live turnover rather than a coach’s call.
regressions: Start the defender closer to goal.
successIndicators: Scan and identify the most dangerous threat.
Delay or prevent the scoring opportunity.
matchApplication: After turnovers, defenders often sprint back towards goal before they can identify opponents. This drill teaches players to combine high-speed recovery with scanning, prioritisation and controlled defensive engagement.

title: Close, Contest and Recover
primarySkill: Recovering immediately after applying pressure or contesting possession.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to close an opponent, affect the disposal and immediately recover into the next defensive action.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Position two attackers in sequence, approximately 10 metres apart.
Place one defender between the attackers but closer to the first receiver.
A feeder begins with the football at the side of the area.
The first attacker presents for possession while the second attacker prepares to receive the next disposal.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder disposes to the first attacker.
The defender closes and applies legal pressure or a controlled contest.
The first attacker then disposes towards the second attacker.
Immediately after the first contest, the defender recovers towards the second receiver.
The defender attempts to pressure, spoil or intercept the next possession.
The attackers score by moving the football through the target gate.
The defender scores one point for affecting either disposal and two points for affecting both.
Reset with the sequence beginning from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Close the first receiver under control.
Apply pressure without losing the ability to recover.
Do not stop to watch the outcome of the first contest.
Turn towards the next threat immediately after the disposal.
Recover through the inside rather than following a wide arc.
Use the first pressure effort to make the next disposal predictable.
Communicate with supporting defenders where available.
Maintain effort through both defensive actions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first close is balanced.
Whether the defender reacts immediately after the disposal.
Whether the recovery route is direct and goal-side.
Whether the first pressure effort influences the second possession.
Whether intensity is maintained through both actions.
Whether the defender remains able to contest the next receiver.
progressions: Add a third consecutive receiver.
Allow attackers to choose between multiple options.
Introduce full match-like tackling.
Reduce the distance between possessions.
Begin with the defender on the ground or out of position.
successIndicators: React immediately after the first disposal.
Recover through a direct goal-side route.
Maintain defensive effort through multiple actions.
matchApplication: Defenders rarely complete only one action in a passage of play. After tackling, spoiling or pressuring a disposal, they must recover immediately to affect the next possession and prevent the opposition from escaping.

title: Inside-Out Chase and Corral
primarySkill: Chasing from an inside position to corral a ball carrier towards the boundary.
objective: Develop players’ ability to recover inside the ball carrier, reduce forward space and guide possession towards a less dangerous boundary position.
groundSize: 35 metres long × 20 metres wide beside a boundary line or marked sideline.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge and one main teaching point
setup:
Mark a narrow channel beside the boundary.
Place one inside scoring gate and one boundary-side scoring gate at the far end.
Position an attacker with a football approximately 25 metres from the gates.
Place a defender two metres behind and slightly inside the attacker.
The attacker begins moving at the coach’s signal.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker accelerates towards the scoring gates.
The defender chases from the inside and attempts to narrow the attacker’s forward path.
The defender does not immediately tackle but closes to a controlled corral position.
The attacker attempts to escape through either gate.
The inside gate is worth three points and the boundary gate one point.
The defender scores one point for forcing the wide gate and two points for preventing any score.
Controlled tackling may be introduced after the movement pattern is established.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Recover inside the attacker rather than directly behind.
Protect the shortest path towards goal.
Close gradually without allowing an inside step.
Use the boundary to reduce the attacker’s available space.
Remain balanced and avoid diving at the football.
Watch the attacker’s hips and football position.
Accelerate when the attacker loses control or slows.
Communicate if a supporting defender is approaching.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender begins from an inside position.
Whether the attacker is prevented from crossing centrally.
Whether the defender closes without overcommitting.
Whether the boundary is used effectively.
Whether balance is maintained through changes of direction.
Whether the defender recognises the correct moment to attack.
progressions: Introduce full legal tackling.
Add a supporting attacker.
Allow the ball carrier to handball or kick.
Increase the channel length.
Begin from a loose football.
regressions: Start the defender level with the attacker.
successIndicators: Guide the attacker towards the boundary.
Recognise when to tackle or force the disposal.
matchApplication: When chasing an opponent in open play, defenders must recover inside and protect the route to goal. A controlled corral can force the ball carrier towards the boundary, delay the attack and allow teammates to recover.

title: Defending the Switch Runner
primarySkill: Tracking an opponent who changes from the ball side to the weak side during a switch.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to recognise, track and hand over an opponent moving across the ground during a change in the direction of possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the area into left, central and right vertical lanes.
Position attackers across all three lanes.
Match defenders to attackers at the start.
Begin with possession in one outside lane.
Nominate one attacker to run from the ball side across to the weak side as the football is switched.
Place three scoring gates at the far end.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins circulating the football on one side.
A nominated attacker runs behind or through the central lane towards the weak side.
The attack switches the football across the ground.
The original defender tracks the runner until a teammate clearly accepts responsibility.
Weak-side defenders adjust centrally before expanding to the new ball side.
The attackers attempt to use the switch runner to score through a gate.
Defenders score one point for completing the handover and two points for preventing the runner’s possession.
Rotate the switch runner and defensive responsibilities after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Scan for opponents moving away from the original ball side.
Track the runner until responsibility is clearly handed over.
Communicate the runner’s name, lane and direction.
Weak-side defenders must prepare to accept the runner before the switch arrives.
Remain goal-side during the handover.
Avoid both defenders following the runner.
Maintain central protection while adjusting to the new ball side.
Pressure the switch kick to reduce its speed and accuracy.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan for the crossing runner.
Whether the original defender maintains responsibility.
Whether the weak-side defender prepares early.
Whether communication is specific and acknowledged.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether the switch runner receives uncontested possession.
progressions: Add a second crossing runner.
Remove the nominated runner and allow attackers to choose.
Introduce full tackling.
Allow the attack to fake the switch.
Begin from an unpredictable turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the runner and switch direction.
Pause play at the handover point.
successIndicators: Identify runners moving across the ground.
matchApplication: Attacking teams often send runners across the ground during switches to create an extra option on the weak side. Defenders must track and hand over those movements without abandoning the centre of the ground.

title: Three-Line Compression Movement
primarySkill: Compressing three defensive lines towards the football while maintaining depth.
objective: Develop coordinated movement between high, midfield and deep defensive lines as the team compresses space around opposition possession.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the defending team into a high line, midfield line and deep line.
Position the attacking team across two-thirds of the ground.
Mark reference bands approximately 18–22 metres apart.
Begin with the attack in controlled possession at one end.
Nominate one communicator in each defensive line.
Place scoring gates behind the deepest line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team moves the football around the area.
When the attack disposes backwards or sideways under pressure, all defensive lines step forward.
When the ball carrier has time and space, the deeper lines adjust backwards while preserving connection.
Each line communicates its movement to the line ahead.
The defensive objective is to keep the playable area compressed around the football.
Attackers attempt to receive between or behind the defensive lines.
Defenders score one point for forcing play backwards and two points for an intercept.
After a turnover, defenders exit through either wide gate.
coachingPoints: Compress the ground when the opposition is under pressure.
Maintain staggered depth rather than three flat lines.
The front line initiates pressure; the middle and deep lines support it.
Move before the next receiver takes possession.
Keep approximately 15–20 metres between lines.
Do not step forward if pressure on the ball is absent.
Communicate the deepest opponent and space behind the structure.
Recover together when the attack breaks pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the lines step forward together.
Whether compression is linked to pressure on the football.
Whether gaps appear between lines.
Whether the deep line protects space behind.
Whether players move before the attacking disposal.
Whether the structure recovers together when pressure is broken.
progressions: Remove the reference bands.
Add full match-like tackling.
Allow long kicks over defensive lines.
Introduce rapid turnovers.
Add a repeat entry after an unsuccessful exit.
regressions: Allow the coach to call “step” or “drop”.
successIndicators: Compress the ground when pressure is applied.
Maintain connected spacing between three lines.
matchApplication: Team defence requires the entire ground to become smaller when the opposition is under pressure. Connected compression removes easy short options, increases intercept opportunities and prevents large spaces opening between lines.

title: Backward-to-Forward Press Transition
primarySkill: Transitioning from a retreating defensive shape into coordinated forward pressure.
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise when the opposition has lost forward momentum and convert a retreating shape into an aggressive connected press.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a gate at each end.
The attacking team begins moving forward with an initial numerical advantage.
Defenders begin in a controlled retreating shape.
Two recovering defenders enter from behind the attack after the first disposal.
The attack is encouraged to use a backwards disposal when forward options are closed.
Explain that a backwards or stationary possession may become the pressing trigger.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attack moves forward while defenders delay and protect central space.
Recovering defenders restore numerical balance.
If the attack disposes backwards, receives facing its own goal or becomes stationary, the nearest defender calls “press”.
The defensive line stops retreating and moves forward together.
The first defender closes the ball carrier while teammates remove short options.
Deeper defenders step to protect space behind the press.
Defenders score three points for creating a turnover within five seconds of the trigger.
Attackers score by breaking the press and passing through the opposite gate.
coachingPoints: Retreat only while the opposition retains forward momentum.
Recognise when numbers have recovered behind the football.
Use backwards possession as an opportunity to step forward.
The press call must be early and decisive.
All defenders must change direction together.
The nearest defender closes under control.
Supporting defenders protect the next disposal.
If the press is broken, recover goal-side immediately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders delay appropriately while outnumbered.
Whether they recognise when numbers are restored.
Whether the press trigger is identified.
Whether the entire line changes direction together.
Whether short exit options are removed.
Whether the team recovers if the press fails.
progressions: Remove the nominated press triggers.
Add full match-like tackling.
Reduce the playing area.
Begin from different numerical disadvantages.
Add a second attacking wave if the press is broken.
successIndicators: Delay while the opposition has forward momentum.
Recognise when defensive numbers are restored.
Change direction as a connected unit.
Create pressure without exposing space behind.
matchApplication: Defences often retreat immediately after turnovers but must recognise when the opposition is forced backwards. That moment allows the team to stop conceding ground, step forward and create a turnover through coordinated pressure.

title: Defensive Rotation After a Mark
primarySkill: Reorganising defensive positions while an opponent holds a mark.
objective: Develop players’ ability to use the time created by an opposition mark to reset match-ups, protect dangerous space and prepare for the next phase.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with three attacking gates at one end.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Begin each repetition with an attacker taking an uncontested mark.
Defenders start in deliberately imperfect positions.
The player on the mark must set immediately.
Remaining defenders reorganise while the marked player prepares to dispose.
howTheDrillWorks:
An attacker takes a mark and the nearest defender sets the mark.
The remaining defenders use the pause to identify opponents and dangerous space.
Defenders rotate into goal-side, cover and deeper positions.
The player on the mark attempts to influence the disposal direction without infringing.
After the umpire-style call of “play on”, the attack attempts to score through a gate.
Defenders attempt to force play wide or intercept the next disposal.
Defenders score one point for completing their reset before play resumes and two points for stopping the attack.
Rotate the starting mark position after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Set the mark quickly and legally.
Use the pause to communicate match-ups and loose opponents.
Protect the corridor and deepest space first.
The closest defender picks up the most dangerous free player.
Avoid all defenders moving towards the mark.
Anticipate the likely disposal from the ball carrier’s position and preferred side.
Prepare to move before “play on”.
If the ball carrier plays on, transition immediately into active pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the mark is set quickly.
Whether defenders communicate during the pause.
Whether loose opponents are identified.
Whether central and deeper space is protected.
Whether defenders anticipate the next disposal.
Whether the group reacts immediately when play resumes.
progressions: Allow the ball carrier to play on immediately.
Remove the coach’s “play on” call.
Add full tackling after play resumes.
Begin with different field positions.
Add a second consecutive mark requiring another reset.
regressions: Use one central and one wide gate only.
matchApplication: An opposition mark provides defenders with a brief opportunity to reset. Teams that use this time effectively can restore match-ups, protect dangerous space and influence the direction of the next disposal.

title: Loose Player Pickup on Transition
primarySkill: Identifying and covering the most dangerous free opponent after a turnover.
objective: Develop players’ ability to recognise loose opponents, prioritise danger and establish defensive accountability immediately after possession changes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with three scoring gates at each end.
Divide players into equal teams.
Begin with one team attacking in one direction.
Place spare footballs with the coach.
At unpredictable moments, the coach calls a turnover or introduces a new football to the other team.
Players must immediately change from attack to defence.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team circulates the football and attempts to score.
The coach calls “turnover” or disposes a new football to the opposing team.
The team losing possession immediately scans for loose opponents.
The nearest defender pressures the ball carrier.
Other defenders identify and cover the most dangerous free players.
Players may exchange opponents through communication rather than returning to original match-ups.
The new attacking team has eight seconds to score through a gate.
Defenders score one point for eliminating all uncontested central options and two points for forcing a turnover.
coachingPoints: React to the change of possession immediately.
Protect goal-side and central space before searching for original opponents.
Identify the opponent closest to goal, corridor or next possession.
Communicate who is taking each loose player.
The nearest defender pressures the football.
Do not have two players cover the same opponent.
Recover through central routes.
Reassess responsibilities after every disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
The speed of reaction after possession changes.
Whether defenders protect central space first.
Whether dangerous loose opponents are identified.
Whether responsibilities are communicated.
Whether players duplicate coverage.
Whether defensive accountability changes as the attack moves.
progressions: Increase the frequency of turnovers.
Add full match-like tackling.
Use multiple footballs in rapid sequence.
Introduce scoreboard consequences.
Expand to two-thirds of the ground.
regressions: Announce the turnover several seconds in advance.
Pause play to confirm defensive match-ups.
matchApplication: After turnovers, players rarely have time to find their original opponent. Effective transition defence requires immediate pressure on the football and rapid coverage of the most dangerous free players.

title: Full-Width Defensive Shift
primarySkill: Moving the entire defensive structure across the full width of the ground.
objective: Develop the coordinated movement required for all defensive lines to shift from one side of the ground to the other without losing central protection or depth.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground using the complete width.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two-thirds or the full ground.
Mark four vertical lanes across the width.
Arrange attackers across all lanes.
Position defenders in high, midfield and deep lines.
Begin with the attack holding possession near one boundary.
Place scoring gates at the far end and defensive exit gates behind the starting point.
Nominate a communicator in each defensive line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team circulates possession on one side.
On the coach’s signal or when an option appears, the attack switches across the full width.
All defensive lines shift towards the new ball side.
Ball-side defenders close the receiver while weak-side defenders move through central cover positions.
The structure must preserve depth behind the pressure.
Attackers may switch back again at any time.
Defenders score one point for completing the shift before the receiver plays on and two points for forcing a turnover.
After winning possession, defenders exit through a gate on the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Begin shifting as the switch is prepared.
Use efficient diagonal running lines rather than following the football’s full path.
Protect the corridor throughout the shift.
The new ball-side line must arrive ready to pressure.
Weak-side defenders narrow centrally before expanding.
Maintain staggered depth across all lines.
Communicate the switch from the deepest line.
Do not exhaust the group by sprinting unnecessarily towards harmless possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether movement begins before the switch arrives.
Whether defenders use efficient running lines.
Whether central protection is maintained.
Whether all three lines shift together.
Whether the new pressure line arrives balanced.
Whether repeated switches create fatigue-based gaps.
progressions: Remove lane markings.
Add full match-like tackling.
Allow long diagonal kicks behind the defensive structure.
Require multiple switches before scoring.
Introduce rapid turnovers during the shift.
regressions: Allow the coach to call defensive movement.
successIndicators: Shift before the football reaches the new side.
Arrive on the new ball side ready to apply pressure.
matchApplication: Teams frequently switch possession across the full width to stretch defensive structures. The defence must shift efficiently, preserve central protection and arrive on the new ball side with enough balance to pressure the next possession.

title: Defensive Movement Under Fatigue Assessment
primarySkill: Maintaining coordinated defensive movement during repeated high-intensity phases.
objective: Assess whether players can sustain the movement, communication and structural discipline developed through TD-021 to TD-039 during repeated match-intensity defensive phases.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Use two-thirds or the full ground.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Arrange defenders across high, midfield and deep lines.
Prepare a sequence of scenarios:
Sprint recovery from out of position
Consecutive pressure efforts
Boundary chase
Full-width switch
Backwards disposal triggering a press
Immediate turnover with loose opponents
Keep spare footballs with coaches around the area.
Assign coaches to assess movement quality, communication and decision making.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins the first attacking phase from a nominated scenario.
The defence attempts to stop the attack and exit the area.
Immediately after the phase ends, the coach introduces another football from a different location.
Defenders must recover, reorganise and respond to the new problem.
Each work block lasts 90–120 seconds and contains three to five separate defensive phases.
Defenders score for stops, forced wide entries, successful presses and controlled exits.
Attackers score for central entries, loose-player possession and goals.
Complete four to six blocks with appropriate recovery and positional rotation.
coachingPoints: Maintain movement technique when fatigued.
Recover through central goal-side routes.
Continue scanning rather than running blindly towards the football.
Preserve spacing between defensive lines.
Communicate more clearly as physical fatigue increases.
Recognise when to delay, shift or press.
Pick up the most dangerous loose opponent after turnovers.
Complete the defensive stop before attempting the exit.
Avoid reckless pressure caused by fatigue.
Reset mentally after each phase.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether recovery routes remain disciplined.
Whether closing footwork deteriorates under fatigue.
Whether defenders continue scanning.
Whether line spacing remains connected.
Whether communication decreases or becomes vague.
Whether players recognise press and delay situations.
Whether loose opponents are identified after turnovers.
Whether second and third efforts remain effective.
Whether exit decisions become rushed.
Whether players reset for each new phase.
progressions: Reduce recovery between work blocks.
Introduce full match-like contact.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure scenarios.
Require the defence to transition into a forward entry after each successful exit.
Allow the attacking team to select the next scenario.
regressions: Use one scenario at a time.
Allow 10–15 seconds for defensive organisation between phases.
Limit contact and focus on movement quality.
successIndicators: Maintain effective recovery routes under fatigue.
Apply the correct delay, press or cover response.
Complete multiple defensive efforts without losing structure.
Secure possession and select an appropriate exit.
Reset physically and mentally for the next phase.
matchApplication: Late in quarters and during repeated opposition attacks, defensive movement quality often deteriorates. This assessment measures whether players can preserve structure, communication and decision making when required to complete several high-intensity defensive actions without a full reset.

title: Tackle, Release and Cover
primarySkill: Coordinating the tackler and surrounding defenders to prevent an effective disposal.
objective: Develop players’ ability to apply a legal tackle while supporting defenders close the likely handball and kick-release options.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Begin with two attackers against three defenders.
One attacker starts with the football and the second provides a release option.
Position one defender as the tackler and two defenders in cover positions.
Use controlled tackling intensity during the first block.
Rotate all players through attacking, tackling and cover roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves towards the target gate.
The nearest defender closes and applies a legal tackle.
The second defender protects the nearest handball release.
The third defender positions behind and inside the contest to cover a loose football or escaped disposal.
The ball carrier attempts to release legally before or during the tackle.
Defenders score one point for forcing an ineffective disposal and two points for winning possession.
If the ball carrier releases successfully, defenders immediately rotate pressure and cover roles.
Reset after a score, turnover or stoppage.
coachingPoints: The tackler must close under control and maintain legal technique.
Supporting defenders should not crowd the tackle unnecessarily.
Protect the most likely release option before attacking the football.
The deepest defender must remain goal-side of the contest.
Communicate who is tackling and who is covering.
Expect the football to spill and prepare to recover it.
Rotate roles immediately if the ball carrier escapes.
Avoid creating a free opponent through two defenders tackling one player.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the nearest defender applies a safe legal tackle.
Whether supporting defenders protect release lanes.
Whether two defenders unnecessarily attack the same player.
Whether a defender remains behind the contest.
Whether players react quickly to a spilled football.
Whether pressure continues after a successful release.
progressions: Add a third attacking release option.
Introduce full match-like tackling.
Begin from a loose football rather than controlled possession.
Allow the attack to kick as well as handball.
Require an immediate defensive exit after the turnover.
regressions: Use tackle bags before live tackling.
successIndicators: Recover loose footballs created by pressure.
Rotate defensive roles after the ball is released.
matchApplication: A tackle is most effective when teammates remove the ball carrier’s escape options. This drill connects individual tackling technique with the surrounding pressure and cover required to force a turnover rather than merely complete contact.

title: Three-Sided Pressure Triangle
primarySkill: Surrounding possession with coordinated pressure from three defensive angles.
objective: Develop a coordinated three-player pressure structure that limits the ball carrier’s forward, inside and release options without overcrowding the contest.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with one central and two wide attacking gates.
Begin with three attackers against three defenders.
The ball carrier starts in the centre with two supporting attackers positioned ahead and to either side.
Position one defender in front of possession and two defenders on supporting angles.
Begin with controlled pressure and no tackling.
Rotate starting roles after every repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier attempts to move through a scoring gate or release to a teammate.
The first defender closes the direct forward path.
The second defender protects the inside release and corridor.
The third defender covers the outside or trailing release.
Defenders adjust the triangle as the ball carrier changes direction.
Attackers may exchange positions but must remain within the area.
Defenders score one point for forcing the ball carrier backwards and two points for a turnover.
Play continues for 15–20 seconds before resetting.
coachingPoints: The first defender must corral rather than dive at the football.
The inside defender protects the most dangerous release.
The third defender closes the remaining practical escape route.
Maintain enough distance to react without leaving passing gaps.
Move the triangle with the ball carrier.
Communicate which direction the pressure is guiding possession.
Avoid all three defenders becoming flat.
Attack the football only when the carrier loses balance or control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders occupy three distinct pressure angles.
Whether the central route remains closed.
Whether the defenders crowd the same space.
Whether the pressure shape moves with the ball carrier.
Whether a defender protects the release behind the first pressure.
Whether the group recognises the correct time to tackle or intercept.
progressions: Add legal tackling.
Add a fourth attacker as a deeper release option.
Reduce the playing area.
Begin from a contested ground ball.
Allow immediate transition after a defensive turnover.
regressions: Mark the three defensive positions with cones.
successIndicators: Deny the corridor and forward route.
Move the pressure shape with possession.
Create turnovers without overcrowding the contest.
matchApplication: Around a ball carrier, effective defenders close multiple escape routes while preserving structure. This drill teaches players to surround possession intelligently rather than having several defenders chase from the same angle.

title: Smother and Spill Recovery Shape
primarySkill: Supporting a smother attempt with organised recovery around the likely spill.
objective: Develop the relationship between pressure on a kicker and supporting defenders positioned to recover the football if the kick is smothered or partially affected.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Position one attacker with the football and a receiver 10–15 metres ahead.
Place one defender close enough to pressure the kick.
Position two supporting defenders to either side and slightly behind the pressure defender.
Use additional groups where numbers allow.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker prepares to kick to the receiver.
The nearest defender closes and attempts a controlled smother.
Supporting defenders move into positions where the football is likely to spill.
If the kick is smothered, all players compete for the loose football.
If the kick escapes, the supporting defenders recover towards the receiver.
Defenders score one point for affecting the kick and two points for winning the spill.
Attackers score by completing the kick and moving through the target gate.
Reset immediately after the possession is resolved.
coachingPoints: Close the kicker from a balanced angle.
Protect the face and keep the body within safe smother technique.
Supporting defenders must expect the football to spill forward, sideways or behind.
Avoid standing directly behind the smothering player.
Communicate who is applying pressure and who is recovering the loose football.
Maintain one defender goal-side of the contest.
If the kick clears the smother, transition immediately into receiver pressure.
Secure the football before attempting the defensive exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the smother attempt is safe and balanced.
Whether supporting players anticipate the spill.
Whether defenders occupy different recovery positions.
Whether one player remains behind the contest.
Whether defenders react if the kick escapes.
Whether the loose football is secured cleanly.
progressions: Allow the attacker to handball or kick.
Add a second attacking receiver.
Begin with the kicker moving at speed.
Introduce controlled tackling after the spill.
Require the defence to exit through a target gate.

Increase the distance to the receiver.
successIndicators: Maintain defensive balance behind the contest.
Recover loose footballs created by the smother.

matchApplication: A smother often creates an unpredictable ground ball rather than immediate possession. Supporting defenders must be positioned to recover the spill while retaining protection if the ball escapes the first pressure effort.

title: Aerial Contest Spill Defence
primarySkill: Structuring defenders around an aerial contest to control the resulting spill.
objective: Develop a coordinated defensive structure around a marking contest so the team can defend the aerial ball and control the ground-level outcome.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a feeder 25–35 metres from a contested marking area.
Place one attacker and one defender in the aerial contest.
Position two attacking ground-level players and three defensive support players around the contest.
Place a scoring gate behind the contest and two defensive exit gates to either side.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles regularly.
Begin with controlled body contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the aerial contest.
The key defender attempts to mark or spoil the football away from the scoring gate.
One supporting defender positions front and centre.
A second defender protects the goal-side spill.
A third defender remains slightly wider as balance and exit support.
Attackers attempt to win the spill and score through the gate.
Defenders score one point for controlling the spoil direction and two points for winning and exiting with possession.
Reset after a score, turnover or completed exit.
coachingPoints: The aerial defender should spoil towards defensive support where possible.
Ground-level defenders must not stand directly under the aerial contest.
Protect the front-and-centre and goal-side spill areas.
Maintain one player outside the immediate contest for balance.
Communicate the intended spoil direction.
Move as the kick travels rather than waiting for the ball to arrive.
Secure the ground ball before beginning the exit.
If the attack wins the spill, apply immediate pressure without losing goal-side cover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the aerial defender influences the spoil direction.
Whether support players position before the contest.
Whether defenders crowd underneath the football.
Whether goal-side space remains protected.
Whether the balance defender supports the exit.
Whether pressure is immediate if the attack wins the spill.
progressions: Add a second aerial attacker.
Introduce full contested marking.
Vary the kick location and height.
Add a repeat entry if the defensive exit fails.
Require the exit to progress beyond a second gate.
regressions: Begin with no aerial body contact.
successIndicators: Control or recover the loose football.
matchApplication: Aerial defence is not complete when the ball is spoiled. Teams must organise around the contest so the spoil is directed towards teammates and the opposition cannot score from the resulting ground ball.

title: Defensive Front-and-Centre Crumb
primarySkill: Winning or neutralising the front-and-centre position at a marking contest.
objective: Teach defenders to recognise and protect the most dangerous front-and-centre ground-ball area beneath a forward marking contest.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Position a feeder 20–30 metres from a marking contest.
Place one attacker and one defender in the aerial contest.
Position one attacking crumber and one defensive crumber front and centre.
Add one defender goal-side of the contest.
Place a scoring gate behind the contest and two exit gates to either side.
Rotate all players through each role.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the marking contest.
The aerial players contest the football.
The defensive crumber establishes front-and-centre position before the ball arrives.
The attacking crumber attempts to win the spill and score.
The goal-side defender protects any football spilling behind the contest.
If the defensive crumber wins possession, they select an appropriate exit gate.
Defenders score one point for neutralising the attacking crumb and two points for winning and exiting.
Reset after each possession.
coachingPoints: Move into front-and-centre position while the football is in flight.
Stay goal-side of the attacking crumber.
Avoid being drawn directly under the marking contest.
Read the likely direction of the spoil.
Use legal body positioning to protect the drop zone.
Keep the hands free and remain ready to collect at ground level.
If possession cannot be won, prevent the attacker from escaping centrally.
Communicate with the aerial and goal-side defenders.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defensive crumber moves before the spill occurs.
Whether goal-side position is maintained.
Whether the player remains balanced at ground level.
Whether the attacking crumber gains a central exit.
Whether the deeper defender protects the back of the contest.
Whether the defensive exit suits the pressure.
progressions: Add a second attacking crumber.
Vary the location of the aerial contest.
Introduce full body contact.
Allow the attacking crumber to begin from either side.
Add a second defensive possession after the first exit.

Give the defensive crumber a positional head start.

Read and attack the likely spill.
Deny a clean central scoring opportunity.
Win, neutralise or safely exit the ground ball.
matchApplication: Forward crumbers are most dangerous when positioned front and centre of a marking contest. Defenders must protect this area before the spill occurs and prevent the opposition from gathering cleanly towards goal.

title: Stoppage Exit Denial
primarySkill: Preventing clean opposition exits from a congested stoppage.
objective: Develop a connected defensive structure around a stoppage that pressures the first possession and denies clean release into open space.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central stoppage circle approximately eight metres in diameter.
Position equal numbers from both teams around the stoppage.
Place four exit gates on the outside of the playing area.
The coach starts each repetition with a ball-up, throw-in simulation or ground-ball release.
Defenders identify a pressure player, inside-cover players and outside balance players.
Rotate starting positions after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football into the central contest.
The attacking team attempts to win possession and exit through any gate.
The nearest defender pressures the first possession.
Inside-cover defenders close short handball lanes.
Outside defenders protect the likely exit routes and remain goal-side.
If the attack exits the first contest, the defence rotates pressure and cover roles.
Defenders score one point for forcing a second stoppage and two points for a turnover.
Attackers score by completing controlled possession through an exit gate.
coachingPoints: Pressure the first possession immediately.
Protect the most dangerous forward and inside exits.
Avoid having every defender enter the initial ground-ball contest.
Outside defenders must remain connected closely enough to close the release.
Communicate the location of free opposition players.
Maintain legal tackling technique in congestion.
If the first handball escapes, rotate rather than stop.
Accept a neutral stoppage when clean possession cannot be won safely.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first possession is pressured.
Whether defenders protect short handball lanes.
Whether all players become drawn into the contest.
Whether outside defenders close the release quickly.
Whether pressure continues after the first handball.
Whether tackling remains safe and legal.
progressions: Allow unrestricted tackling.
Add a numerical advantage to the attacking team.
Reduce the distance to the exit gates.
Introduce different stoppage starting positions.
Continue into a larger transition area after the exit.
regressions: Increase the size of the area.
Pause after the first possession to identify defensive roles.
successIndicators: Deny clean inside and forward exits.
Maintain cover outside the immediate contest.
Force turnovers, rushed disposals or repeat stoppages.
matchApplication: Opposition teams seek clean exits from stoppages to break defensive lines before structures can reset. This drill teaches defenders to pressure the first possession while protecting the release lanes around the contest.

title: Repeat Tackle Pressure Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining pressure through several consecutive attacking possessions.
objective: Develop defenders’ ability to complete repeated pressure actions and transfer responsibility as the football moves through a handball chain.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a rectangular area with a target gate at each end.
Begin with four attackers against four defenders.
Attackers start in a staggered handball chain.
Match defenders to the first four attacking positions.
The attacking team attempts to advance through repeated handballs.
Rotate roles after each 30–40-second repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker receives the football and is immediately pressured.
The attacker attempts to handball to the next runner.
The nearest defender transfers pressure to the new ball carrier.
The original pressure defender recovers inside and becomes cover for the next contest.
The sequence continues through multiple attacking possessions.
Defenders score one point for affecting a disposal and three points for a turnover.
Attackers score by exiting through the target gate.
If the football becomes loose, play remains live until possession is secured.
coachingPoints: Complete the first pressure action before moving to the next role.
Recover inside immediately after the football is released.
The nearest defender pressures the new ball carrier.
Supporting defenders protect the next handball receiver.
Maintain legal tackle technique despite fatigue.
Do not stop after missing a tackle.
Communicate each transfer of pressure.
Preserve one balance defender behind the chain.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders transfer pressure quickly.
Whether the original tackler recovers after the release.
Whether the next receiver is closed before accelerating.
Whether tackling technique deteriorates under repeated effort.
Whether a balance defender remains behind the play.
Whether players continue after a missed tackle.

Add full match-like tackling.
Reduce the width of the area.
Begin from a ground-ball contest.
Add a second attacking wave after the first gate.
regressions: Increase the distance between defenders and attackers.
successIndicators: Transfer pressure to each new ball carrier.
Recover after completing a tackle or close.
Maintain defensive roles throughout the chain.
Force rushed handballs, spills or turnovers.
matchApplication: Opposition teams often attempt to escape pressure with consecutive handballs. Effective defence requires repeated efforts, rapid role changes and pressure on every receiver rather than one isolated tackle.

title: Outnumbered Contest Clamp
primarySkill: Containing an outnumbered ground-ball contest until support arrives.
objective: Teach defenders to prevent a clean attacking release from an outnumbered contest by protecting central space, slowing possession and creating time for support to arrive.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations and several observable behaviours
setup:
Begin with three attackers against two defenders around a loose football.
Position two recovering defenders 10 metres behind the starting contest.
Place one central and two wide scoring gates at the attacking end.
The central gate is worth more than the wide gates.
Rotate players through starting defender, recovering defender and attacker roles.
Begin at controlled intensity.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach rolls or throws the football into the contest.
Three attackers attempt to win possession and exit through a scoring gate.
The two starting defenders protect the central route and pressure the first possession.
They avoid overcommitting to the ground ball if clean possession cannot be won.
Recovering defenders sprint through inside positions to join the contest.
Once support arrives, the defence increases pressure and attempts to win possession.
Attackers score three points centrally and one point through a wide gate.
Defenders score one point for delaying until support arrives and two points for a turnover.
coachingPoints: Protect the central exit before attacking the football.
One defender pressures while the second protects the likely release.
Stay on the feet where possible.
Force possession sideways or backwards.
Recovering defenders must enter through goal-side central space.
Communicate when support has arrived.
Increase pressure only when the defensive numbers improve.
Accept a stoppage rather than allowing a clean attacking exit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders protect the central gate.
Whether one defender remains outside the immediate ground-ball contest.
Whether the first possession is slowed.
Whether recovering defenders use inside routes.
Whether pressure increases when support arrives.
Whether the attack is forced wide or into congestion.
progressions: Begin with four attackers against two defenders.
Increase the recovery distance.
Add full match-like tackling.
Allow attackers to kick after winning possession.
Continue into an open transition phase after the contest.

successIndicators: Protect the central route while outnumbered.
Remain balanced outside the ground-ball contest.

matchApplication: After turnovers and broken contests, defenders are often temporarily outnumbered. The correct response is to clamp dangerous space and delay the release until teammates recover rather than attempting a low-percentage immediate win.

title: Forward-Half Turnover Pressure Wave
primarySkill: Applying immediate collective pressure after losing possession in the forward half.

coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction

Use the attacking half of the ground.
Position one team in an attacking structure and the other in defensive 50.
Place one central and two wide exit gates near the centre line.
Begin each repetition with an attacking entry or shot at goal.
The defending team gains possession through an intercept, loose ball or coach-directed turnover.
The original attacking team immediately becomes the pressing team.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team enters inside 50 and attempts to score.
When possession changes, the original attackers react immediately into team defence.
The nearest player pressures the new ball carrier.
Teammates close short exit options and protect the corridor.
Higher players compress towards the turnover while retaining cover behind the press.
The opposition attempts to exit through any gate.
The pressing team scores three points for regaining possession inside 50 and one point for forcing a wide exit.
The exiting team scores three points for a central exit and one point for a wide exit.
coachingPoints: React to the turnover before appealing, stopping or watching.
The nearest player must pressure the first possession.
Protect the corridor and central exit first.
Close the nearest safe release options.

whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
The speed of reaction after possession changes.
Whether the first ball carrier is pressured.
Whether short exit options are removed.
Whether the corridor remains protected.

Reduce the distance to the exit gates.

Protect the corridor and short exits.

title: Defensive Pressure and Contest Assessment
primarySkill: Applying coordinated pressure and contest principles across repeated match-like phases.

Rotate teams through attacking and defending roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each repetition from one prepared scenario.
The attacking team attempts to retain possession, exit or score.
The defence applies pressure while maintaining cover and balance.
After any tackle, spoil or smother, the football remains live.
Defenders must recover spills, close release lanes and reorganise after each disposal.
After a defensive turnover, the team attempts a controlled exit.
Each repetition lasts 45–90 seconds.
Complete six to eight repetitions before teams exchange roles.

Maintain legal tackle and contest technique.

Preserve goal-side balance around every contest.

progressions: Use full match-like contact appropriate to the playing group.
